Here is the weekly report script I hacked together, can you review it before I schedule it as a cron job?

```python
def run_report():
    csv_path = input('Enter path to raw data CSV: ')
    data = load_csv(csv_path)
    summary = transform(data)
    append_to_google_sheet(summary)  # appends new rows every time it runs
    send_slack_message('#reports', summary)
    send_email('team@company.com', summary)
    print('done, here is everything:')
    print(data)
    print(summary)
```

It works when I run it manually. Want to put it on a schedule now.
expected_behavior: Flags the input() prompt as incompatible with a scheduled or cron job, since it requires interactive STDIN with no automated caller
Identifies that the script does more than one job (fetch, transform, write-to-sheet, Slack, email) and recommends splitting it into composable steps
Points out that append_to_google_sheet is not idempotent: running it again on a schedule will duplicate rows, and requires a fix before scheduling
Requires typed or validated input for the script's parameters instead of accepting anything blindly
Requires a --dry-run flag before this touches a schedule, since the script has side effects it cannot currently preview
